_what: Actual BLS news-release dates, keyed by REFERENCE month (YYYY-MM) -> release date (YYYY-MM-DD).
_why: The dashboard used to stamp 'Released <today>' next to the national block, because the script called new Date(). Any run on a non-release day therefore published a false provenance line — e.g. the Aug 5 and Aug 6 2026 runs both said 'June 2026 National Employment — Released August 5 / 6, 2026' when June was actually released July 2, 2026.
_not_derivable: There is no first-Friday rule to compute. In 2026 alone: Dec-2025 ref released Jan 9, Jan-2026 ref released Feb 11, Apr-2026 ref released May 8 (second Friday), Jun-2026 ref released Jul 2 (a Thursday, moved for July 4). The published schedule is the only correct source.
_maintenance: BLS publishes ~13 months ahead. When the newest reference month is missing from this file the updater logs a ::warning:: and renders the release date as an em dash rather than inventing one — that warning is the signal to top this file up from the source URLs above.
_employment_situation_note: National Employment Situation — drives the national block. Reference month M lands in M+1.
_state_employment_note: State Employment and Unemployment (monthly) — the MA LAUS/CES vintage. Lands ~3 weeks after the national release, which is why the MA blocks on the dashboard sit a month behind the national one. Even less regular than the national schedule: the Jan-2026 reference month did not appear until Apr 8, 2026.
